answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a mesa as the anchor of the cost.
